name: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum
role: Ruler of Dubai (2006–present), Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE (2006–present)
summary: Hereditary ruler of Dubai who has driven a state-led, trade-open development model built around free zones, state-owned flagship companies, and national strategies such as UAE Vision 2021 and Centennial 2071. His public statements stress tolerance, women's roles in government, technology, space and innovation, and a managerial style of government. His record on political freedoms has drawn criticism from rights groups and UK court rulings, which are not treated here as his stated positions.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: He rules Dubai by inheritance from his brother and decreed his own son heir, keeping the office in the family.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Announced the UAE Net Zero by 2050 initiative, saying the UAE is committed to cement its climate leadership and backing it with over AED600 billion of renewable investment, framed as an economic opportunity; he has not used language of drastic measures.

dynastic-succession.rationale: As Ruler he decreed his son Hamdan Crown Prince of Dubai in 2008 (Decree No. 4 of 2008), passing the succession to his child.

elective-rulers.rationale: He holds the rulership of Dubai by hereditary succession, not election, and appointed a son as heir by decree.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He publicly welcomed the Barakah nuclear plant as the region's largest clean energy source and an environmental contribution.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Law No. 7 of 2006 restricts ownership to UAE and GCC nationals in general but lets the Ruler grant foreigners freehold in designated areas, so he opened land ownership to non-citizens rather than barring it.

free-trade.rationale: He presented the UAE as a free-market economy open to trade without constraints and urged the GCC to ease cross-border trade restrictions.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: He issued Law No. 24 of 2006 creating a public body to advance women into leadership roles and approved the Gender Balance Index for government bodies.

public-ownership.rationale: He founded government-owned Dubai World to run ports, airports and free zones, and the government-owned Investment Corporation of Dubai to supervise state companies.

rent-control.rationale: Decree No. 43 of 2013 caps rent increases at lease renewal across Dubai by comparison with the average rent of similar units.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Law No. 11 of 2006 sets up a government corporation that follows a strategy for investing Dubai government assets across financial, industrial and service sectors.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Law No. 11 of 2013 makes health insurance compulsory for nationals and residents, with the government enrolling nationals and employers or sponsors enrolling others, so coverage is legally guaranteed for all.

notes: Thin, mostly official-media record. Answers rest on laws and decrees he issued as Ruler of Dubai (Dubai Legal Portal) and a few statements. Themes searched: government and succession, property and housing, health, economy and state companies, gender, energy, trade. His books and sheikhmohammed.ae are listed in notFound. Federal measures only signed or approved in cabinet (e.g. the 2020 Israel agreement) were not counted. Court findings about Princess Haya and Pegasus were not treated as his positions. Two earlier answers were nulled: one rested on a book review's second-hand quotes, the other mixed words with actions. Statements added since 2026-10-23 were checked against these records and are null where nothing settles them.
